rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 6 line 52, 'The loop that started with a failing test closed.' 'The loop' is never named inside THIS file before line 52, but the rule's module-include-order clause makes the enclosing module's What You'll Learn signposting count as prior context: getting-going.md line 16 (before the '## Start here' includes, i.e. before this exercise's own content in deck order) reads '**Run** an orient -> fix -> close -> compound loop end-to-end on a trivial bug in your own repo' -- the four-phase loop is introduced there, and 'the loop' is a standard definite-article callback to it. (The arc-earned-spine-vocabulary carve-out does NOT independently apply -- getting-going.md is M1, so there is no prior module to have earned it in; and getting-going.md's Key Concepts bullet 'The loop is orient -> fix -> close -> compound' at line 57 sits AFTER the Start-here includes per module-shape.md's own placement rule, so it is NOT prior-in-deck-order and cannot be cited as the resolving antecedent -- correcting a mis-citation in the prior instance, which pointed at getting-going.md line 114, itself below that file's line-92 maintainer cut and never student-facing.) Chunk 0/1's 'the bug you fixed' (lines 5, 13) and chunk 3's 'the PR' (expanded prompt, line 39) resolve under the session-artifact carve-out. Chunk 4's 'it' (line 43) is immediate continuation of chunk 3's close-out subject. Chunk 5's 'the next agent' (line 48) is generic future-session phrasing needing no specific antecedent. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Only external pointer in body: chunk 3 line 35, '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)' -- named by the document's own title ('Adding a connector is one command per tracker'), not located by page position. Satisfies the navigational-pointer carve-out. `grep -niE '(the opening|the prior|earlier (lecture|exercise|module))' curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--close-the-ticket.body.txt` -> 0 hits: no backward callback to another file by position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0/1's 'the bug you fixed'/'the bug's ticket' (lines 5, 13) and chunk 3's expanded-prompt 'the PR' (line 39) resolve against fix-tests-first.md. Verified via getting-going.md's '## Start here' include order (lines 44-50): orient-and-introspect.md -> fix-tests-first.md -> close-the-ticket.md -> compound-and-close.md, so fix-tests-first (which ships the PR) is the exercise immediately preceding this one. This file's own Arc section states 'Picks up from: fix-tests-first -- the shipped PR is what the close-out links to,' matching the module structure. No dead beat references found.

Shortest chunk is 4 ('Double-check the voice', lines 41-44): its one bullet ('Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it.') is a self-sufficient compare-and-correct instruction, not a bare wait-state. All seven chunks (incl. title) carry a self-contained instruction or claim.

Checked all six body headers against chunk content: 'Read the ticket for your bug' -> opens+pastes ticket link (11-19); 'Read the conventions off the ticket' -> field-convention read + five-rule ask (20-31); 'Write the close-out and send it' -> drafts+posts close-out (33-40); 'Double-check the voice' -> register check (41-44); 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' -> generalises the move, declarative per rule 15's own named exception for this exact heading (45-49); 'What happened' -> recap (50-55). No header contradicted by its own chunk content.

`grep -niE '\bnot\b' curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--close-the-ticket.body.txt` -> 2 hits (line 23 'not the policy', line 47 'you did not write') -- single negations, no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: none found on a full read. Self-grading-superlative sub-item (blocking): closest line is chunk 3 line 35, '...and it pays back on every session after this one' -- a persistence claim about the connector install, not graded/superlative language; stays inside. Number+retraction: none ('20 minutes', 'five bug rules' are plain unhedged counts). Abstraction-noun stacks: none -- vocabulary stays concrete (ticket, tracker, connector, close-out, comments). Empty-leg verb triplets: none found.
